provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)
provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: External validity is limited: the findings are from one large program in Beijing, and the report argues the paper should better characterize the MMP (what makes it successful, what greenery is used) so policymakers can judge whether results transfer to other settings.
issues.quote: the paper would benefit from the authors expanding on the external validity of the findings from Beijing

issues.text: The paper does not empirically characterize the greening beyond its location within MMP areas; it lacks information on tree types, whether trees were saplings or mature, and whether they are native or well-adapted to Beijing, which limits understanding of what drives the results.
issues.quote: there isn't much on empirically characterizing the greening (beyond that it's in the MMP areas), discussion of the types of trees planted, or what greening may have worked best

issues.text: It is unclear whether the observed greening is clustered (new urban forests) or scattered, and whether this matters for the pollution and pollen results; the report suggests the authors consider upwind greening measures that capture spatial concentration rather than averages.
issues.quote: How concentrated/clustered is the observed greening? Is this important for the results?

issues.text: The NDVI measure may capture only certain types of vegetation growth; the report questions whether the change reflects extensive or intensive margin changes, and how this relates to the forest-versus-scattered question.
issues.quote: Is the change in NDVI capturing certain types of vegetation growth?

issues.text: The paper does not sufficiently discuss background PM2.5 and pollen levels and allergy sensitivity, which matter for transferring the cost-benefit conclusions to other geographies.
issues.quote: I was wondering whether they could do more to discuss background pollen levels and allergies

issues.text: Figure 3 omits 95% confidence intervals for the pre-MMP estimates, making it hard to assess those estimates; the evaluator asks for them to be shown, perhaps in an appendix.
issues.quote: Why are 95% confidence intervals not shown for the pre-MMP estimates in Figure 3?

issues.text: The contrast in Figure 5 between PM2.5 persisting over multiple days and pollen not doing so is not explained; the evaluator asks whether this is consistent with the science literature.
issues.quote: Based on Figure 5, PM~2.5~ "sticks around" for longer

issues.text: Pollution and pollen monitors differ in number, coverage and time period (35 pollution stations for 2014-2019 versus 12 pollen monitors for 2013-2016), and few pollen monitors are in the city center; the evaluator suggests discussing these differences and running a robustness check on close-by pollution/pollen pairs.
issues.quote: pollen count data is only for 12 monitors for 2013-2016

issues.text: The payback period of the program is not stated explicitly, which the evaluator thinks would help practitioners.
issues.quote: it might be nice to state the payback period of the program explicitly for practitioners

issues.text: The introduction does not define the unit 'mu' used for the Million Mu Project, which may confuse readers unfamiliar with it.
issues.quote: It might be helpful to define in a footnote in the second paragraph of the introduction what *mu* is

issues.text: Figure 1 uses very similar light green colours for the -0.01 to 0 and 0 to 0.01 ranges, which the evaluator finds confusing as both suggest greening.
issues.quote: I found it a tiny bit confusing that in Figure 1, the -0.01 to 0 and 0 to 0.01 colors were both in some very light green

issues.text: The NDVI labels and colouring do not reappear on Figure 4 part b), which the evaluator suggests they should.
issues.quote: The NDVI labels/coloring could appear again on Figure 4, part b).
